name: Ringer mode, Do Not Disturb and Focus
plain: Android shows ringer mode and DND state freely; iOS exposes only a Focus on/off flag after a prompt.
meaning: Reveals when the person does not want to be disturbed: sleeping, working, driving. Android leaks more with no prompt; iOS gates it behind a Focus Status permission and returns one boolean.

android.note: DND state readable with no permission since API 23; policy details need Notification Policy Access

ios.api_surface: Returns true, false or nil only; the physical ringer switch and Focus name are not exposed

limits.headline: Can see ringer and Do Not Disturb on Android, but only Focus on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing on Android. On iPhone you answer a permission prompt first
can: See if your Android is on normal, vibrate or silent
See if Do Not Disturb is on, on Android 6 and newer
See on iPhone if a Focus is on, after you allow it
Hold back sounds or alerts to match your mode
cannot: See the name of your iPhone Focus
See the position of the iPhone ringer switch
Change Do Not Disturb on Android without Notification Policy Access
Learn which calls or contacts you let through
limits.differs: Android shows ringer and Do Not Disturb with no prompt. iPhone shows only on, off or unknown after a permission prompt.

story.what_it_is: An app can see if your phone is on silent or in a Do Not Disturb mode.

marketing.name: Focus status
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps can ask permission to know only if a Focus is on, with no detail about which one.

story.for_you: On Android, apps can see your ringer mode and Do Not Disturb with no prompt. On iPhone, an app must ask first and only learns a simple yes or no. It can hint when you sleep, work or drive.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to avoid noisy alerts at bad times, and to show Away status in chat. Because it reveals your routine, Apple keeps it behind a prompt and a single yes or no.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows you as Busy when you turn on a Focus, so friends know you will not reply.
A game mutes sound effects when your phone is on silent but keeps vibration.
A workout app changes alerts to haptics when the ringer is off.
A driving app learns you are in a driving Focus and reads messages aloud.
A work app holds low priority alerts when you are in a work Focus.
An ad firm reads silent mode as a sign you are at a meeting or in bed.

story.android_note: Ringer mode and Do Not Disturb state are readable with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Needs a Focus Status permission and returns one yes or no flag.

technical_bounds: iOS never exposes which Focus is active
Needs the person to grant Focus Status once

legit_uses: Messaging apps show a Focus status

history.change: INFocusStatusCenter added with a user prompt
